headline_marked: [[Iran closes Strait of Hormuz]] after attacking 'unauthorized' ship; warns of 'harsh response'
headline: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz after attacking 'unauthorized' ship; warns of 'harsh response'
summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard announced the closure of the vital Strait of Hormuz, claiming it attacked and stopped a ship violating maritime security. Tehran warned of a "harsh response" to any retaliatory measures.
details: Iran's Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) announced on Sunday the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping lane. This action followed their claim of attacking and stopping a ship that was allegedly operating without authorization and disrupting maritime security.

The IRGC stated that the vessel had turned off its identification system and ignored warnings while attempting to cross the strait through an "unauthorized path." They did not provide specific details about the ship involved in the incident.

Tehran has issued a stern warning, stating that the Strait will remain closed "until further notice" and "until the end of US intervention in the region." They also threatened a "harsh response" to any aggression against Iran, including targeting enemy bases.

In response, senior US officials had previously urged Iran to publicly commit to stopping attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The US also called for all waterways in the strait to remain open for navigation without any tolls.

Despite escalating conflict in the Gulf region, US President Donald Trump stated on Friday that both the US and Iran had agreed to continue discussions, simultaneously announcing an end to a ceasefire. A senior Iranian source indicated that Iran, the US, Qatar, and Pakistan had agreed in principle to hold talks.

Oman has been playing a mediating role in the conflict, with its Foreign Minister meeting Iran's Foreign Minister to discuss ensuring safe passage through the Strait. Oman has reportedly proposed a draft plan for free navigation through its southern corridor and requiring prior Iranian approval for ships in the northern corridor without tolls.

The closure comes amidst a wider conflict in the Gulf, which began after joint US-Israeli airstrikes on Iran on February 28, leading to a surge in global energy prices. The Strait of Hormuz is crucial, historically transporting nearly one-fifth of the world's total oil supply.

headline_marked: [[Former Speaker Barrister Zamiruddin Sircar passes away]] at 94 in Dhaka
headline: Former Speaker Barrister Zamiruddin Sircar passes away at 94 in Dhaka
summary: Barrister Zamiruddin Sircar, former Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad and acting President, passed away at 94 due to age-related complications. He was a prominent figure in Bangladeshi politics.
details: Barrister Zamiruddin Sircar, former Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad and former acting President, passed away. He breathed his last at 4:19 AM on Sunday (July 12) while undergoing treatment at a hospital in Dhaka. He was 94 years old and had been suffering from various age-related complications.

Born on December 1, 1931, in Nayabari village of Tetulia Upazila, Panchagarh district, Barrister Sircar had a long and distinguished career. His contributions to the nation's parliamentary democracy are widely recognized.

He served as the Speaker of the Eighth Jatiya Sangsad, playing a crucial role in the legislative process. Additionally, he briefly held the position of acting President in 2002, demonstrating his commitment to national service.

Throughout his political life, he was associated with the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) for a significant period. His involvement greatly influenced the country's parliamentary system and law-making procedures.
caption:
Barrister Zamiruddin Sircar, a towering figure in Bangladeshi politics and former Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad, has passed away at the age of 94.

Barrister Zamiruddin Sircar, former Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad and former acting President, passed away. He breathed his last at 4:19 AM on Sunday (July 12) while undergoing treatment at a hospital in Dhaka. He was 94 years old and had been suffering from various age-related complications.

Born on December 1, 1931, in Nayabari village of Tetulia Upazila, Panchagarh district, Barrister Sircar had a long and distinguished career. His contributions to the nation's parliamentary democracy are widely recognized.

He served as the Speaker of the Eighth Jatiya Sangsad, playing a crucial role in the legislative process. Additionally, he briefly held the position of acting President in 2002, demonstrating his commitment to national service.

Throughout his political life, he was associated with the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) for a significant period. His involvement greatly influenced the country's parliamentary system and law-making procedures.
